paragraphs: On Thursday morning, it rained a lot. Mia stood at Lily's door without an umbrella. "Can I share yours?" she asked. "Of course," said Lily. "Mom wants us to take the bus today, because the road is wet." The bus was crowded, so the girls stood near the door. Lily closed the umbrella, and Mia held her bag tight. The rain made a loud noise on the roof of the bus. Lily smiled, because she liked the sound of the rain.

"What is our timetable today?" asked Mia. "English first, then math, then science," said Lily. "The club is after lunch." "Math again?" said Mia. "I am not good at math." "Which subject do you like best?" asked Lily. "I like art and science," said Mia. "Science is about animals, and I love animals." "I like English," said Lily, "because I write for the blog in English."

"Did you do the math homework?" asked Lily. "I did half of it," said Mia. "The last two questions were too hard." "Teacher Kim gives us daily homework," said Mia. "It is too much!" "It is only ten minutes," said Lily. "And you are smart, Mia." "Am I?" asked Mia. "I am smart in science, but not in math." "Then I will probably help you," said Lily.

The bus stopped at the school gate, and the rain was still strong. Lily opened the umbrella, and the girls ran under it. "I am sorry that I forgot my umbrella," said Mia. "It is fine," said Lily. "Anyway, I like to share." Their shoes were quite wet when they came into the hall. Mia's bag was wet, too, but her homework was dry.

At lunch, the girls sat in the library with the math book. Lily read the first question, and Mia wrote the answer. The last question was hard, so they read it three times. Then Mia smiled and said, "I see it now!" She wrote the answer and checked it. "It is right," said Lily, "and you did it alone." Mia laughed. "So I am smart in math, too!"
